overview: Activity on bpf-next for September 13-14 was focused and light. Leon Hwang posted a v2 improving bpftool to compute light skeleton map sizes at runtime rather than baking them in at compile time. Kumar Kartikeya Dwivedi submitted a v2 fix series bounding ownership depth through local kptrs and graph roots to close a gap in acyclic ownership enforcement in the verifier.

patches.title: bpftool: Compute map size of light skeletons at runtime
patches.author: Leon Hwang
patches.summary: This patch changes bpftool to compute the map size for light skeletons dynamically at runtime rather than embedding a fixed size at code-generation time. Previously the size was calculated once during skeleton generation and hard-coded into the output, which could become stale or incorrect if map parameters changed. By deferring the computation to runtime, light skeletons become more robust and correct across different kernel configurations. This is the second revision of the patch, incorporating review feedback.

patches.title: bpf: Bound ownership depth through local kptrs and graph roots
patches.author: Kumar Kartikeya Dwivedi
patches.summary: This patch introduces a bound on the ownership depth reachable through local kptrs and graph root structures to ensure the acyclic ownership check in the BPF verifier terminates correctly. Without a depth bound, a maliciously or inadvertently constructed ownership chain through nested local objects could cause the verifier's cycle-detection pass to run indefinitely or overflow its stack. The fix adds a maximum depth constant and returns a verification error when the limit is exceeded, protecting verifier integrity. This is patch 1 of 2 in the 'Fix acyclic ownership checks' series (v2).

patches.title: selftests/bpf: Check local object ownership depth
patches.author: Kumar Kartikeya Dwivedi
patches.summary: This patch adds selftests to exercise and verify the new ownership depth bound introduced in the companion kernel patch. The tests construct BPF programs that create local objects with varying ownership chain depths, confirming that chains within the limit are accepted and those exceeding it are rejected by the verifier. Covering this case with dedicated tests ensures the depth-bounding logic stays correct across future refactors. This is patch 2 of 2 in the 'Fix acyclic ownership checks' series (v2).
